source_text: ............................................. ........... licet facere fimbriam unam. Iam caro <Deu>s erat, in qua Dei uirtus agebat. Quid, quod prophetae canunt, inuisibilem esse uidendum, Ut claritas tanta fieret homo quoque pro nobis. Nec populus noster prosilisset in noua lege, Si non Omnipotens ordinasset ante de nobis. Hic erat Omnipotens, cuius <in> nomine gentes Credere omnino, quod propheta dixit Esaias: Exurget in Israel homo de radice Iesse In illum sperabunt gentes, cuius signo tuentur. Et alter dixit testem illum esse per orbem Manifestari eum principem nationibus ipsum. In psalmis canitur: Dominus regnauit a ligno; Exultet terra, iocundentur insulae multae. Sic et patriarcha Iacob: benedictio uera Paruit in gentes; hic erit spes gentium, inquit. Sub caelo non aliud nomen est nisi Christi praelatum, In cuius nomine crediderunt gentes ubique. Non ita suademur credere pro tempore passo Sed propter futurum tempus in aeterno uiuentes. Haec speranda nobis spes est sempiterno frunisci Non ista, quae fragili<s> cito mutat gaudia nostra. Sint licet diuitiae prae oculis laute fruendae Excluderis illis substituta morte caduca; Aut si perseuera[ue]ris, horrescis ipse uiuendo Aut si ualetudo fuerit mala, quo tibi uita? Tormentum est totum, quo uiuimus isto sub aeuo; Hinc adeo nobis est spes in futuro quaerenda: Hoc Deus hortatur, hoc lex, hoc passio Christi, Ut resurrecturos nos credamus in nouo saeclo. Sic Dei lex clamat: fieret cum humilis Altus, Cederet infernus, ut Adam leuaretur a morte Discendit in tumulum Dominus suae plasmae misertus Et sic per occulta inaniuit fortia mortis. Obrepsit Dominus ueteri latroni celatus Et pati se uoluit, quo magis prosterneret ipsum. Ille quidem audax et semper saeuus ut hostis, Dum sperat in hominem saeuire, uictus a Summo est. Per quod prius hominem prostrauerat morti malignus,
pass_a_gloss: Lacuna initio. Iam caro Deus — uirtus Dei. Inuisibilis uidendus; claritas homo pro nobis. Isaias radix Iesse; gentes sperabunt. Dominus regnauit a ligno. Nomen Christi. Spes in futuro / resurrectio. Dominus in tumulum — mortem inanit; latronem ueterem uincit.
pass_b_english: …one may make a single fringe. Already flesh was God, in which God’s power was at work. What of this — that the prophets sing the invisible is to be seen, so that such brightness should also become man for us? Nor would our people have sprung forth in the new law if the Almighty had not ordered it beforehand concerning us. This was the Almighty, in whose name the nations were wholly to believe, as the prophet Isaiah said: A man will rise in Israel from Jesse’s root; the nations will hope in him, by whose sign they are kept. And another said he is a witness through the world — that he himself, a prince, be shown to the nations. In the psalms it is sung: The Lord has reigned from the wood; let the earth exult, let many islands be glad. So too patriarch Jacob: a true blessing appeared among the nations; this will be the hope of the nations, he says. Under heaven no other name is set forward except Christ’s, in whose name the nations everywhere have believed. We are not so urged to believe for a time of suffering, but for a future time, living in the eternal. This hope is to be hoped by us — to enjoy everlasting hope — not those joys our fragile state soon changes. Though riches be before the eyes richly to be enjoyed, you are shut out from them, a frail death put in their place; or if you last, you yourself shudder while living; or if health is bad, what is life to you? The whole in which we live under this age is torment; hence indeed hope in the future must be sought for us: this God urges, this the law, this Christ’s passion — that we believe we will rise in a new age. So God’s law cries: when the High One became humble, hell would yield, so that Adam be raised from death. The Lord went down into the tomb, pitying his own fashioned clay, and so through hidden things he emptied death’s strong things. The Lord crept on the old robber, hidden, and willed to suffer so that he might more throw him down. That one indeed bold and always savage as an enemy, while he hopes to rage against a man, was beaten by the Highest. Through what the malign one had first thrown man down to death — ****** Flesh was already God at work. Nations hope in Jesse’s root; the Lord reigns from the wood; he enters the tomb to empty death.
